slice.question: Can the current Gumbel-Softmax / mirror-descent / primal-dual link family be compacted into a cross-field transfer contract with explicit temperature/schedules, feasibility gates, assumptions, one conflict-free portable action rule, and exact evidence scope?
slice.answer: Yes as a scoped synthesis contract, but not as a new convergence theorem. The ingredients have separate primary/authoritative support; their unified gated rule below is an inference/design contract whose guarantees inherit only when each ingredient's source assumptions hold.

portable_transfer_contract.name: hard-gated entropic primal-dual categorical selector
assumptions: A finite candidate/action set is available at each decision point.
Each candidate has a comparable scalar utility or loss contribution and measurable constraint residuals.
A hard feasibility predicate can be evaluated before action execution; at least one feasible action exists or an explicit safe fallback is defined.

For any convergence claim, the objective/constraint/saddle structure must satisfy the convexity, boundedness, step-size, and regularity assumptions of the cited optimization result; no such guarantee is claimed for arbitrary nonconvex cross-field use.
Temperature is strictly positive while a relaxed categorical representation is used.
portable_transfer_contract.hard_feasibility_gate: m_i(t)=1 only when candidate i satisfies all non-negotiable feasibility/conflict/authority gates at t; otherwise m_i(t)=0. Mask m_i=0 candidates before normalization and never execute them. If sum_i m_i(t)=0, execute the predefined safe fallback and skip relaxed choice.
portable_transfer_contract.penalized_score: z_i(t)=u_i(t)-lambda_t^T r_i(t), where u_i is the comparable utility score and r_i is the vector of soft/resource constraint residuals. This score form is part of the synthesis, not a theorem quoted from the Gumbel papers.
portable_transfer_contract.temperature_schedule: tau_t=max(tau_min, tau_0*rho^t), with tau_0>tau_min>0 and 0<rho<1. This geometric schedule is an explicit portable design choice. The Gumbel-Softmax source supports smooth annealing toward categorical behavior, but does not establish this particular schedule as universally optimal.
portable_transfer_contract.relaxed_policy: For feasible candidates only, y_i(t)=softmax_i((log w_i(t)+G_i)/tau_t), G_i iid Gumbel noise. Use this only when differentiable relaxed exploration/training is useful; the final execution gate remains hard.
portable_transfer_contract.entropic_mirror_update: w_i(t+1) proportional to m_i(t)*w_i(t)*exp(eta_t*z_i(t)), followed by normalization on the feasible simplex. A portable diminishing choice is eta_t=eta_0/sqrt(t+1); this particular schedule is a design default, not a universal convergence claim.
portable_transfer_contract.dual_update: lambda_{t+1}=Proj_{R_+^k}(lambda_t+gamma_t*r(a_t)), e.g. gamma_t=gamma_0/sqrt(t+1) as a portable default. This is a projected primal-dual/subgradient-shaped synthesis; source-specific convergence conditions must be checked before claiming rates.
portable_transfer_contract.single_conflict_free_action_rule: After applying the hard feasibility mask, execute exactly one candidate a_t=argmax_{i:m_i(t)=1}[log w_i(t)+z_i(t)/tau_t], with a fixed deterministic tie-breaker. Never execute a masked candidate. The optional Gumbel relaxation can train/update weights, but execution is deterministic so concurrent conflicting actions are not sampled.
portable_transfer_contract.safe_fallback: If no candidate passes the hard gate, perform no candidate mutation and persist the exact blocker/continuation instead of weakening feasibility.

evidence.title: Categorical Reparameterization with Gumbel-Softmax
evidence.scope_supported: Differentiable relaxation of categorical samples and smooth annealing toward a categorical distribution.
evidence.scope_not_supported: Does not by itself justify the hard feasibility gate, the proposed geometric temperature schedule, mirror update, dual update, or unified execution rule.

evidence.title: The Concrete Distribution: A Continuous Relaxation of Discrete Random Variables
evidence.scope_supported: Continuous reparameterizable relaxation of discrete random variables on a simplex and low-variance biased gradient use in the stated settings.
evidence.scope_not_supported: Does not establish the unified gated primal-dual contract or universal cross-field convergence.

evidence.title: Mirror descent and nonlinear projected subgradient methods for convex optimization
evidence.scope_supported: Mirror descent as a nonlinear projected-subgradient method and an entropic mirror-descent algorithm over the unit simplex with convex-optimization efficiency analysis.
evidence.scope_not_supported: Does not validate arbitrary nonconvex categorical gating or the exact synthesized temperature/dual schedules.

evidence.title: A first-order primal-dual algorithm for convex problems with applications to imaging
evidence.scope_supported: First-order primal-dual optimization for convex problems with saddle-point structure; source reports convergence to a saddle point and O(1/N) rate in its finite-dimensional nonsmooth convex setting.
evidence.scope_not_supported: Does not establish convergence of this synthesized hard-gated Gumbel/mirror selector outside its stated convex saddle-point assumptions.

evidence.title: Subgradient Methods
evidence.scope_supported: Primal-dual subgradient formulation for constrained convex optimization and projected/dual updates under the notes' assumptions.
evidence.scope_not_supported: Teaching-note support for update shape only; it is not evidence that the complete synthesized selector has a new convergence theorem.

directly_supported: Gumbel/Concrete differentiable categorical relaxation and annealing concept.
Entropic mirror descent on the probability simplex for convex optimization.
Primal-dual first-order/subgradient methods for constrained convex or saddle-point problems under source assumptions.
synthesis_inference_only: The specific geometric temperature schedule tau_t=max(tau_min,tau_0*rho^t).
The specific 1/sqrt(t+1) portable step-size defaults in the combined rule.
The exact penalized-score composition and deterministic tie-broken argmax execution rule.
Any claim that the full combined contract inherits convergence outside the intersection of source assumptions.
